# 1.2.39 - the map is yours again, and a body no longer starts Stage 7

**The map takes clicks.** Found, and it was ours. `layerIndex()` in `glass.mjs`
promoted Foundry's `#interface` to `position: relative; z-index: 1` so the
interface would never go under the glass. It needs that promotion - without it
parts of the UI paint beneath the curtain - but a positioned full-screen box
that still takes pointer events is a lid, and every click meant for the map
landed on it. The layer is ours to pay for: `#interface` is made transparent to
the pointer and every child that was hit-testable is pinned back to `auto`, so
not one control changes behaviour and the board gets its clicks back. If
anything else ever puts a lid there, the same repair fires on its own -
probed at four points, because the middle of the screen is where a window sits.
`drpgGlassDebug()` now prints the whole hit stack over the map.

**Notices are tilted again.** 1.2.38 made the notice tile a constant of the
glass, and a constant is not measured - so no rotation was written for the
stack and the cards stood upright inside a tilted pane. The tilt is keyed to
the selector and computed from the fixed box, so it holds even though the tile
is never measured and the stack does not exist until the first card arrives.

**Windows are the size of their content.** Two causes. Nothing ever measured a
window without a table in it (`fitWindowToTable` returned early), which is why
raising the Look window's width did nothing; it now measures the overflow and
grows by exactly that much, and only ever grows. And the base sheet pins every
prose dialog at 544 px with `!important`, which no inline width can outrank -
under the theme those windows are `fit-content`, floored at exactly what they
are today so none can get narrower, capped at a readable measure so prose
settles instead of running to the edge. The clock and Despair explainers, whose
prose is capped at 46 characters, get a lower floor so the frame fits the card.

**The glow stays through a colour change.** It was hidden for the length of the
turn, so the light along every seam vanished and came back - the one thing on
screen that says "glass". The old bloom is snapshotted beside the ghost and the
two cross over, so the light changes colour without ever leaving.

**The objection cut.** Three things were wrong and none was the duration, which
is why lengthening it twice changed nothing. It was found inside the pulse
scan, and `loop()` gates that behind the glass-pulse setting - with the pulse
off it never fired at all. Two flashes shared one canvas and one removal, so
whichever ended first took the other's light with it. And it sat below the
morph's own layers. It is watched before the gate, owns its canvas, paints
above everything, and rises, holds and releases on a cubic ease over 1400 ms
with a bloom under the line.

**A body no longer starts the Investigation.** Finding one used to move the
phase on the spot, mid-scene. It writes a record instead: the card stands, the
music is paused where it stood, and Daily Life carries on until the GM starts
the Investigation or moves the time of day on. Two facts, not one - "a body has
been found" holds until Stage 7 starts (it is what stops the same corpse being
announced twice and what ends the killer's fresh-scene discount), while "found
this hour" goes stale by its own stamp, which is what ends the silence. The GM
panel's Next line says what is owed and carries the button. Themes without the
Event panel get a row on the clock instead. A latent defect goes with it: the
body card read an incident record that `endMurder` wipes before the GM presses
anything, so in the ordinary flow it never appeared at all.

**Project icons are choosable again.** Each project takes a glyph from the
module's own set - 21 of them, the hourglass still the default - stored on the
project and drawn as a mask in the interface's state colour, so a project's
icon changes colour with everything else on the glass. Each is named by the
Font Awesome icon the module already maps, so the picker draws correctly under
both themes with no new sprite work. Projects made before this go on showing
the hourglass, pixel for pixel.

Also: the pane under something waiting really does beat faster now. The field
that says so has been written since 1.2.27 and read by nothing.
